description: The line plot illustrates the relative change in performance across different layers for various token-precision configurations in KV cache compression, with the x-axis representing five layer ranges—Layer1-4, Layer5-12, Layer13-20, Layer21-28, and Layer29-32—and the y-axis showing the relative change in performance from -25% to +5%. The baseline is a dashed gray line at 0%, representing the performance of a 4×tokens, 4-bit configuration. The yellow line with circular markers, labeled "LB-Avg of 2×tokens,8-bit," starts at approximately 0.5% relative change for Layer1-4, dips to around -1% for Layer5-12, rises to about 0.2% for Layer13-20, slightly increases to 0.3% for Layer21-28, and ends at 0.4% for Layer29-32. The red line with square markers, labeled "LB-Avg of 1×tokens,16-bit," begins at 0.2%, decreases to -3.5% for Layer5-12, drops further to -5.5% for Layer13-20, rises to -1% for Layer21-28, and ends at 0.1% for Layer29-32. The light blue line with circular markers, labeled "RULER4k of 2×tokens,8-bit," starts at -1.5%, decreases to -3.5% for Layer5-12, drops to -12% for Layer13-20, rises to -1% for Layer21-28, and ends at -1% for Layer29-32. The dark blue line with square markers, labeled "RULER4k of 1×tokens,16-bit," starts at -4%, decreases to -6% for Layer5-12, drops to -25% for Layer13-20, rises to -6% for Layer21-28, and ends at -4% for Layer29-32. The plot shows that the performance of the 1×tokens,16-bit configurations (red and dark blue lines) generally declines more sharply than the 2×tokens,8-bit configurations (yellow and light blue lines), especially in the middle layers, with the dark blue line showing the most significant drop in performance.
